Mārīca, nevertheless, he must be asked something agreeable by us. Ho there! Who is there? (Entering) Disciple: Venerable sir, here I am.

Mārīca and Gālava, go now through the air and, at my word, convey this pleasant news to the venerable Kaṇva: that Śakuntalā has become a mother, and that Duṣyanta, having regained his memory upon the cessation of the curse, has accepted her.
“As the Blessed One commands,” the disciple replied and departed.
“O child Mārīca, you too, together with your children and wife, quickly mount the chariot of Ākhaṇḍala and set out for your capital.”
"As the Blessed One commands, O King; and furthermore, Mārīca,
may Indra grant abundant rain upon your subjects."
You too, having prepared the sacrifice, gratify the Wielder of the Thunderbolt;
thus, for hundreds of cycles of ages, may you both conduct yourselves through mutual duties that are praiseworthy for their benefit to both worlds. //34//
"O Blessed One, I shall strive for my welfare according to my ability.
"O son Mārīca, what further favor may I do for you? "O King, there is nothing more dear than this: if the Blessed One [is pleased] here."
If you wish to do so, then let it be thus:
may the king proceed with his benedictory verse for the welfare of his subjects; may Sarasvatī, the goddess of speech, be honored by those of great learning;
and may the blue-and-red Lord Śiva also bring an end to my worldly existence.
The Self-born One, his power spent regarding rebirth, has departed; all have gone forth.
Thus ends the seventh act.
Thus ends this drama named *Abhijñānaśākuntalam*.
